title: Micro-prime oscillation worklog: priming effects on tail latency
content:
Goal:
- Quick experimental log to probe short (100-200ms) priming probes and their effect on tail latency for 8k-context model runs. Trying to reproduce intermittent p99 spikes we've seen on Dedicated pools when cold-ish KV caches mix with small warmup sequences.

Hypothesis:
- Small repeated priming (3-10 tokens, done in bursts before real requests) biases runtime scheduling and can either (a) reduce p50/p90 by pre-initializing KV pages or (b) amplify p99 due to pipeline interference. Expect non-monotonic behavior as prime frequency increases.

Environment / config:
- Fleet: dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (nvlink disabled, mixed gpus: A10G/GV100)
- Model: open-variant-13b-8bit (quantized weights, float key/value cache)
- Runtime flags: continuous-batching=true; kv-cache-prefetch=off (baseline), then on for experiment 3
- Concurrency per worker: 6
- Ingress shape: synthetic Poisson arrivals, avg QPS=45, bursts up to 180 for 2s every 20s
- Payload: typical chat request 350 tokens context + generation 256 tokens

Experiment matrix (short runs, ~10 minutes each):
- A: no priming (control)
- B: prime 5 tokens once per request (inline)
- C: burst priming: 10 tokens sent 200ms before request arrival (shadow header)
- D: priming heartbeat: 3 tokens every 5s per client socket (background)
- E: same as C but kv-cache-prefetch=true

Runs summary (representative numbers, median of 3 runs):
- A (control): p50=82ms, p90=145ms, p95=210ms, p99=470ms, dropouts=0.6%
- B (inline 5t): p50=88ms, p90=150ms, p95=230ms, p99=520ms, dropouts=0.9%
- C (burst pre-req 10t): p50=78ms, p90=140ms, p95=195ms, p99=810ms, dropouts=1.8%
- D (heartbeat priming): p50=85ms, p90=148ms, p95=205ms, p99=560ms, dropouts=1.1%
- E (burst + prefetch): p50=75ms, p90=136ms, p95=190ms, p99=420ms, dropouts=0.4%

Quick ascii sketch (p99 vs priming mode):
- Control  ---------|||||| (470ms)
- Inline  ---------||||||||| (520ms)
- Burst    -------||||||||||||||||| (810ms)
- Heartbeat ------|||||||||| (560ms)
- Burst+Prefetch -|||||| (420ms)

Observations / notes:
- Burst priming (C) reduced lower quantiles slightly (p50 down ~7ms) but produced large p99 outliers and more dropouts. Looks like scheduling collisions: pre-requests create a transient KV churn that occasionally triggers long stalls (seen as >1s tail events).
- Enabling kv-cache-prefetch (E) returned best overall numbers and lowest dropouts — hypothesis: explicit prefetch lets runtime reorder/migrate KV pages ahead of execution without interfering with active request scheduling.
- Inline priming (B) adds overhead on the critical path and slightly worsens tails — avoid inline micro-primes.
- Heartbeat priming (D) is safer than burst but still slightly worse than baseline.

Telemetry hints (what I checked):
- Trace snippets: long p99 traces show repeated io_wait + mmap_page_faults spikes right before heavy token generation; correlated with priming burst timestamps.
- Scheduling: samples show a small subset of workers hit GC-like stall (python gc/arena?) — need lower-level kernel trace to disambiguate.
- Kernel logs: occasional NVLINK errors/timeouts (rare), not correlated across runs.

Unresolved / TODO:
- Re-run C/E with stricter isolation: single-worker-only run to test whether inter-worker eviction is the root cause (target date: 2024-10-09).
- Capture perf-top + eBPF stacktrace for p99 traces to confirm whether page faults are user-space or kernel page-in.
- Try priming with 1-token vs 3-token vs 10-token in burst to find knee point.
- Check whether larger models (33B) show same pattern (hypothesis: worse p99 due to bigger working set).
- Add a config knob to allow async prefetch in runtime (spike-safe path).

Decisions / quick takeaways:
- Do not recommend customer-facing burst priming by default. If customers want priming, prefer controlled prefetch mechanism (E-style) implemented at runtime level.
- Short-term mitigation: enable kv-cache-prefetch on fleets experiencing similar p99 spikes and monitor dropouts for 48h.

Reference links / tickets:
- Linear: REDW-1023 (investigate priming tailcases)
- PR: infra#487 (kv cache prefetch prototype)
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread (link above)

Scratch notes (raw):
- saw 1.6x p99 when bursts aligned with autoscaler micro-slice (maybe burst overlap -> admission window clog)
- sampling rate of telemetry might hide fast 200ms spikes — increase sampling for next run
- consider replacing heartbeat priming with passive keepalive (no token) to avoid KV churn

If anyone wants to co-run: ping me in Slack, can reserve pool-3 for 30m slots.

-- Ankur
summary: Short exploratory worklog showing burst priming can worsen p99 unless combined with prefetch. Recommends runtime-level prefetch and adding traces to confirm page fault source.
